$comment: ★★ A COMMON BESIDE cl's SELECT-ANY DEFINITION OF ITS NAME: THE DEFINITION REPLACES THE COMMON (P69 send-back 5, review-xa4 MINOR 4; D-LK-COMMON-OUTRANKED-A-WEAK-DEFINITION-IN-EVERY-FORMAT) -- the PE documents' `commonYieldsTo: nonOverridableDefinition` (a select-any definition is not an overridable one), on the reference compiler's own objects. The two objects named to the link are cl's builds of `int dss_tentative; int dss_read_tentative(void) { return dss_tentative; }` -- cl writes every C tentative definition as a COMMON, an undefined external whose value is its size -- and of `__declspec(selectany) int dss_tentative = 5;`, a COMDAT select-any DEFINITION, cl's spelling of a definition that may be stated more than once. ✔MEASURED 2026-10-08 (the same main.c built by cl; link.exe 14.44.35228 and lld-link 19.1.5): in both object orders the definition replaces the common and the program reads 5, exit 42; the common object alone reads 0, exit 37. GNU ld answers the opposite for the GNU spelling of such a definition -- a weak one never replaces a common (`examples/c/common_beside_a_weak_definition_elf`, and on this very format `examples/c/common_beside_a_weak_definition_pe_mingw`) -- which is why the answer is a key of the format document rather than a rule of the link, and, for a definition whose own spelling yields, a fact its object states. main.c is DSS's; the 37 it adds keeps either answer apart from the exit code of a program that did nothing. The `release` arm pins that optimizing the DSS half changes nothing about which of the two the program reads.
